issues.location: #crosslang > More 'language by language' > ul.xw-facts, bullet 'How many readers met “genocide” as fact' (page_template.html ~1307; numbers from build_page.py crosswiki_data expo)
issues.problem: These shares come from the cross-wiki marker heuristic, not from the hand-coded voice the page uses everywhere else. That heuristic counts any sentence with 'genocide' and no attribution word as own voice (crosswiki/cards.md, Voice card caveat: 'a marker heuristic, not a coded reading'). So the bullet contradicts the page's own headline and grid. It says 4% of Hebrew readers met genocide 'as fact', yet the H2 and the matrix (§) say Hebrew mentions it only as South Africa's court case. That court-case sentence carries no attribution marker, which is how it gets counted. French shows 9% while its grid cell is attributed (“→“), Dutch 7% while it is disputed (?), and Portuguese only 1% although Portuguese is one of the three editions the H2 says state it as fact. An Israeli outlet could quote 'Hebrew Wikipedia told readers Israel commits genocide', which would be false by this page's own coding. The key-article sets also differ by edition (en 8, he 6, it 5; cards.md 'What the cross-wiki tier covers'), so the shares are not comparable.
issues.fix: Remove the bullet, or recompute it from hand-coded voice: the langs.json headline_claim 'latest' per Gaza genocide (else Gaza war) article, weighted by that article's views. If kept as is, retitle it 'How many readers met a “genocide” sentence with no attribution word' and add: 'Word-marker heuristic, not our coding: it counts court-case and reported mentions too, such as Hebrew’s South Africa suit, and each edition’s key-article set differs.' Then drop the Hebrew figure, or footnote it: 'Hebrew: the court-case sentence only.' Also add the cross-check to the build's chk list so the bullet cannot disagree with cells['gen'].

reviews.notes:
DESK VERDICT: We would run this as a lead weekend digital feature, plus a 60-90 second TV explainer built from three graphics: the #zionism chips (re-establishment struck out, colonization added), the #oct7 Hamas timeline with the 'Militant → military' chip, and the #reads box. The hard condition is issue 1: verify the ArbCom items against primary pages and strip the VERIFY comments. Until then the 'documented on both sides' line cannot go on air as Wikipedia's own finding.

SUGGESTED HEADLINE: Wikipedia now says Israel “began committing genocide” and that Zionism came “through colonization”

SUGGESTED DEK: A revision-by-revision study of English Wikipedia, 2021-2026. 1948 is now “ethnic cleansing … by Zionists”, Hamas lost “militant” five days after October 7, and the hostages have never been in the first sentence of the October 7 article. The change sits in the most-read pages; the average article did not move.

SUGGESTED FIRST THREE PARAGRAPHS (verified page content only):
(1) The Israel article on English Wikipedia, read 4.6 million times in the last 12 months, now states in Wikipedia's own voice: “After the Hamas-led October 7 attacks, Israel began committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.” The next sentence is Israel's denial. In January 2021 and in July 2023, none of the 150 most-read opening sections on the subject charged Israel with genocide. Today seven sentences do, and two of them, in the Israel and Benjamin Netanyahu articles, say it as fact. The Netanyahu article carries no denial.
(2) The rewrite reaches the subject's foundations. In 2021 Wikipedia defined Zionism as “the re-establishment of and support for a Jewish state in the territory defined as the historic Land of Israel”. It is now a movement “to establish and support a Jewish homeland through colonization in the region of Palestine”. Since June 2024 “colonial” or “colonization” was written into that sentence 44 times and taken out 41 times, and 37 of those removals were undone. The Nakba is now “the ethnic cleansing of Palestinian Arabs by Zionists”, while the 1948 Palestine war article still says, naming no one, that “Hundreds of thousands of Jews fled or were expelled from Arab states”.
(3) October 7 itself is “a series of coordinated armed incursions” in the article's first sentence. Across 107 versions, “massacre” stood there for about an hour in total and the hostages never, although the article's own short description says “armed incursions and massacres”. The change is concentrated: one in ten of the subject's most important articles gained terms such as genocide, apartheid or colonial, against 4.4% on other conflicts, while the thousands of minor pages did not move. Wikipedia's arbitration committee documented organised canvassing on both sides [after primary-page check]. Our tests found no campaign footprint, though they could only have seen a large one, and no account carried a term from one language edition to another.

BOTTOM-LINE VERDICTS:
- Good as is: zionism, charge, oct7, crosslang (add the Spanish clause), organised (the new cross-language clause strengthens it), reads, limits.
- Acceptable: against. Optional tweak: 'Not everything moved one way: Jewish ties to the land were kept, and the settlements article added Israel’s position, “but Israel disputes this”.' The current wording leads the counter-trend example with 'illegal under international law'.
- Replace (exact text in the issues): news, board, palestine, reach, when.

NARRATIVE-LED CHECK: 9 of 11 main H2s lead with Israel's story. #when ('One wave: editing rose…') and #board are process headlines, which is acceptable for those sections. The #reach H2 ('The articles the world reads first on Israel changed') is borderline mechanics and acceptable.

- Still open: H1, masthead/byline/chips, the #news and #board bottom lines, #reads placement, the #oct7 then/now strip, and the ArbCom primary-page check (open since round 1).
